### Fixed
- **Every agent turn ended 3 s late: the actors could not reach the OTLP gateway, and the Go ADK's pre-response trace flush spent its full deadline on every turn** (giantswarm/agent-platform#456; gazelle, 2026-09-14, nine of nine turns). The kagent controller sets `KAGENT_PRE_RESPONSE_TRACE_FLUSH=true` on Substrate actors (a checkpoint runtime has no later export window), so the Go ADK force-flushes a turn's spans before the A2A response closes, with a detached deadline of `KAGENT_TRACE_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS` (3 s by default). The actors' exporters point at the OTLP gateway kagent.otel names (`http://otlp-gateway.kube-system.svc:4317`), but the connectivity chart's `substrate-atenet-egress` policy — the actors' egress allow-list, since every connection an actor opens leaves through Substrate's egress gateway — opened nothing towards it: every flush ran into `traces export: context deadline exceeded` at exactly +3.000 s, then the checkpoint, then the controller's `SendStreamingMessage` closed; the caller (Swarmgeist's ✅, the portal's receipt) saw a one-word answer "done" 3.3–3.6 s after the text. The actors' log exporter was broken twice over: the controller forwards only its tracing variables to the actors, so the Go ADK's built-in log exporter (HTTP, `/v1/logs`) posted to the gRPC port and every batch ended in `EOF`. Three changes, one path: (1) the connectivity chart opens the OTLP gateway on the egress gateway and — through the same helper, `agent-platform.kagent.otlpEgress` — on the kagent controller's egress policy, one rule per distinct destination of the kagent.otel signals that are on, selecting the pods of the endpoint's namespace (`<svc>.<ns>.svc[.cluster.local]`) on the endpoint's port (kube-system on 4317 by default, once for both signals; a second endpoint a second rule; an endpoint that is not a Service address the `cluster` entity on its port, as the controller's rule was for every endpoint before); nothing when both signals resolve off. (2) The platform Harness's env (`kagent.harness.env`) gains `OTEL_LOGGING_ENABLED=true` — the Go ADK exports the actors' logs over gRPC to the tracing endpoint instead of the HTTP fallback — and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS=X-Scope-OrgID=giantswarm`, the tenant header the controller sends and deliberately keeps from the actors; the meta chart drops the former when kagent.otel.logging resolves off and the latter when both exporters do (`agent-platform.shape.dropEnv`, the rule the controller's header already followed). (3) `KAGENT_TRACE_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS=500` on the Harness caps the flush: an in-cluster export takes tens of milliseconds, and a slow or unreachable collector can now cost a turn half a second, not three. `make verify-actor-telemetry-egress` asserts the rules (both policies, the default, a second endpoint, the port following the protocol, both signals off, `auto` off without the monitoring API, one signal on, the kubernetes flavour rendering no Substrate egress policy); `tests/verify-kagent-harness.py` the env in every exporter state. The lab renders no network policies (kind runs no Cilium): the policy is render-verified and live-verified on gazelle (`hubble observe --verdict DROPPED` on the egress gateway stays empty during a turn); the flush cap is lab-verified against an unreachable collector. Substrate's own telemetry (the `ateom` worker's periodic `failed to upload metrics: … dial tcp [::1]:4317`, `substrate.otel.endpoint` unset in the meta chart, the atelet OTLP relay socket absent on a worker that started before its atelet) is a separate finding, not on a turn's path — a follow-up issue.
